slot.brief: Two parallel wires with given currents; find net field at a point midway or at a specified location

stem: Two long parallel wires, $20$ cm apart, carry currents of $3$ A and $6$ A in the same direction. A point lies on the line joining them, $10$ cm from the $3$ A wire on the side away from the other wire. The net magnetic field there is (take $\frac{\text{μ}_0}{2\text{π}}=2.0\times10^{-7}$ T m A$^{-1}$)

verdicts.working: The point is 0.10 m from the 3 A wire and 0.30 m from the 6 A wire. Outside the wires, their fields point the same way, so B = 2×10⁻⁷(3/0.10 + 6/0.30) = 1.0×10⁻⁵ T = 10 μT.

working:
Distances from the wires: $r_1=0.10$ m, $r_2=0.30$ m.
The point is outside both wires, so their fields are in the same direction.
$B=\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi}\left(\dfrac{I_1}{r_1}+\dfrac{I_2}{r_2}\right)$
$=2.0\times10^{-7}\left(\dfrac{3}{0.10}+\dfrac{6}{0.30}\right)$ T
$=1.0\times10^{-5}$ T $=10\ \mu\text{T}$.

Independent check: The point is 0.10 m from the 3 A wire and 0.30 m from the 6 A wire. Outside the wires, their fields point the same way, so B = 2×10⁻⁷(3/0.10 + 6/0.30) = 1.0×10⁻⁵ T = 10 μT.
solution:
The point lies outside both wires, so the magnetic fields add. Using $B=\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi}\left(\dfrac{I_1}{r_1}+\dfrac{I_2}{r_2}\right)$, with $r_1=0.10$ m and $r_2=0.30$ m,
$$B=2.0\times10^{-7}\left(\frac{3}{0.10}+\frac{6}{0.30}\right)=1.0\times10^{-5}\text{ T}=10\,\mu\text{T}.$$
